newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's outgoing lawmakers fire new parting shot.
newsitem.headline: HK's outgoing lawmakers fire new parting shot.

text.p: Hong Kong's dying colonial legislature made a symbolic last-ditch plea for democracy on Thursday, calling for changes to the constitution that comes into force when Beijing takes control of the British territory.
Even though it goes out of existence in five days' time, the 60-member legislature voted to amend the Basic Law, or mini-constitution promulgated by Beijing, to speed up universal suffrage.

"According to the current Basic Law, Hong Kong may not have an organ for broad-based direct vote by the year 2007...Hong Kong will be under 'half democratic, half autocratic' rule," said Tsang Kin-shing, the Democrat who proposed the amendment.
The vote has no legal binding and the motion did not propose detailed amendments.
Pro-Beijing legislator David Chu, who is a member of the provisional legislature that replaces the colonial parliament, said Hong Kong was better served by a elitist system.
"One-man-one-vote results in politicians catering to the lowest denominator," Chu said.
Outside the parliament, about 30 protesters demanded cheaper housing as legislators rushed to pass a flood of bills before ending their final session under British rule, probably on Friday.
